title: kate-ui: bind cmd-d and cmd-alt-bracket
summary: command_for_binding maps cmd-d to Command::SelectNextOccurrence and cmd-alt-[ to Command::ToggleFold. Escape still removes the secondary cursors. The two commands exist in kate-core from the earlier packets of this wave.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. The file has no GPUI import, but kate-ui tests run in the rust (macos-15) job and the Mac lane owns crates/kate-ui.

definitions.definition:
/// cmd-d is SelectNextOccurrence and cmd-alt-[ is ToggleFold.
fn edit_binding(name: &str) -> Option<Command>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Add the two arms to edit_binding after f5. normalize_binding already writes modifiers in the order used by the other arms; check the test output for the exact spelling of cmd-alt-[. The test cmd_d_and_cmd_alt_bracket_are_bound asserts command_for_binding("cmd-d") is Some(Command::SelectNextOccurrence) and command_for_binding("cmd-alt-[") is Some(Command::ToggleFold). The existing binding tests stay green. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.
